frameworks.name: 10-Stage Roadmap to $100M+
frameworks.definition: A systematic progression through 10 growth stages with defined constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps, broken down by eight business functions (applicable across software, product, service, and retail).

claims.text: The entrepreneurs who are best rewarded allocate the most resources toward the fewest things that get the highest returns, not toward doing 100 tactics.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: focusing resources on high-return activities compounds faster than spreading effort across many tactics
bounded_by: Does not mean having only one action; means focusing resources to ensure one primary outcome succeeds from multiple angles

claims.text: Strategy at its core is the prioritization of resources; if the business is not growing despite working every day, you are picking the wrong priorities.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: resource allocation determines growth more than total effort; misalignment of effort to return opportunity is the primary growth blocker

claims.text: Setting one clear annual goal (e.g., launch a book and hit $100M, or launch an advisory practice) provides more leverage than maintaining a large goal list; one thing done right makes everything else secondary.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: singular focus prevents diffusion of effort and enables resource consolidation from multiple angles
bounded_by: Applies to founder-led organizations and strategic initiatives

claims.text: Taking one day with a portfolio company should result in clarity on one action item to execute, not a to-do list; the goal is opportunity selection, not tactic enumeration.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: clarity on priority reduces cognitive load and enables resource concentration

claims.text: The 10-stage roadmap from zero to $100M+ has been completed by less than 1% of companies, and it applies across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar models.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: recognizable stage transitions allow systematic progression and constraint diagnosis

examples.text: Alex Hormozi's personal goal-setting practice: one goal per year (e.g., launch a book and hit $100M revenue, or launch an advisory practice). Each year builds on the previous year's clarity. This contrasts with founders who maintain pages of notes with multiple competing priorities.

When working with portfolio companies for a day-long intensive, the output is not a comprehensive to-do list but a single clear priority that the founder can execute from multiple angles (calling friends, hiring help, doing work personally) to ensure success.

practices.text: When you have a large list of potential actions, identify and commit to only one, two, or three priorities that will drive the highest returns; then allocate all resources from multiple angles (personal effort, hired help, external partnerships) to ensure those few things succeed.

Download and follow the 10-stage zero-to-$100M roadmap as a framework for understanding which constraints and functions your business is currently bottlenecked on (available free at acquisition.com/roadmap).
